patch_description: Keep the direct-demand reward, but make two-hop path couplings sensitive to the estimated load on their component links. A chain that can carry meaningful demand is rewarded when its links have light direct demand; the reward is reduced, and can become a penalty, when the chain would send traffic through already heavily demanded links. This retains useful routing structure without applying the same unconditional two-hop reward to every path. The chain terms number at most n(n−1)(n−2), within the quadratic-term limit. Raising the degree penalty also makes exact-degree solutions more attractive before repair.
